From the beginning of January until approximately 2–3 days ago (around two to three weeks), I experienced a persistent cough. I initially developed a cold early in the new year, and the cough never fully resolved. On the 13th of January, I contacted your practice and was informed that a telephone consultation with a GP would be arranged for me one week later.
On the day of the appointment, I received a call early in the morning which I was unable to answer, and it was not clear where the call was coming from. I later received a text message stating that the call had been made by a nurse. When the appointment was booked, I was clearly informed that the call would be from a doctor, not a nurse.
I would also like to clarify an issue that occurred in August last year, which I believe illustrates a broader concern. At that time, I initially attended the practice with significant eye symptoms. I was seen by a GP who attempted to arrange a referral. Later the same day, I was contacted by the practice and informed that I would need to wait until specialist appointments became available and that I would be contacted in due course.
As my symptoms were concerning, I subsequently attended the hospital emergency department myself, where I was assessed by the ophthalmology team and formally diagnosed with Horner’s syndrome.
A few days after this diagnosis, I returned to the practice wishing to discuss the condition with a GP. However, I was again booked to see a nurse, without being informed in advance that the appointment would not be with a doctor. During that consultation, the nurse was unfamiliar with Horner’s syndrome, which further reinforced my concern that this was not an appropriate setting for follow-up of a newly diagnosed neurological condition.
I would like to emphasise that I fully respect the role and contribution of nurses within the NHS. My concern relates specifically to the following points:
When I request to see a GP, I am repeatedly booked with a nurse without being informed beforehand that the appointment will not be with a doctor.
In situations involving uncommon or potentially serious diagnoses, such as Horner’s syndrome, I believe it is reasonable to expect review and follow-up by a GP rather than a nurse-led appointment.
To be clear, my concern is not that the nurse did not recognise Horner’s syndrome. Rather, it is that I was not given the opportunity to see a GP, nor was I informed in advance about the nature of the appointment.
I hope this feedback can be taken into consideration to improve transparency and ensure appropriate clinical triage and communication with patients in the future",null,[0,234]]]],[],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sCi9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21VMmVFTXpjRnBJVkZwZmIxSmFSM05QVlhsb1pGRRAB!2m1!1s0x0:0xcbb28a3b8a9fa48d!3m1!1s2@1:CAIQACodChtycF9oOmU2eEMzcFpIVFpfb1JaR3NPVXloZFE%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT21VMmVFTXpjRnBJVkZwZmIxSmFSM05QVlhsb1pGRRAB&t=1&&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwikn_yIkrGTAxXoMGMBHW4eBVQQoykIBCgB"],null,[null,[[1,0]]]],"0ahUKEwikn_yIkrGTAxXoMGMBHW4eBVQQ0pMFCAIoAA"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFBUnBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEZGZURUZOWjNKZlgxOWZSV2hEVDBkME1FbG5iMFpFZFZablJ6VnZUVUZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVEpSTkVOWlgxZHRZVzA0V1VGRFNVRQ=="],[["Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2xJM1J6WkpVeTFoWlcxTk4xTTRNVmRHVEc5dmRuYxAB",["0x0:0xcbb28a3b8a9fa48d",null,1761555509326736,1761555509326736,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/109806709404803539471/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Esther Adesina","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocI4Q7w3sc0J9Fp4i6r8ORXV-uMAVQPFpWWBO-kTsW40RFQI71o=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/109806709404803539471?hl=en"],"109806709404803539471",null,2,0,null,[0,2,1],0,["2 reviews",null,null,null,null,[null,"0ahUKEwikn_yIkrGTAxXoMGMBHW4eBVQQ7LoGCAYoAA"]]]],null,"4 months ago",null,null,null,null,null,null,["Google","https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/product/1x/googleg_48dp.png",null,null,5],null,1],[[2],null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,["en"],[["The receptionist and the nurses are fantastic, unfortunately I think the GP is confused. would like to provide some feedback regarding my experiences with your practice, particularly in relation to appointment allocation and referral handling.
From the beginning of January until approximately 2–3 days ago (around two to three weeks), I experienced a persistent cough. I initially developed a cold early in the new year, and the cough never fully resolved. On the 13th of January, I contacted your practice and was informed that a telephone consultation with a GP would be arranged for me one week later.
On the day of the appointment, I received a call early in the morning which I was unable to answer, and it was not clear where the call was coming from. I later received a text message stating that the call had been made by a nurse. When the appointment was booked, I was clearly informed that the call would be from a doctor, not a nurse.
I would also like to clarify an issue that occurred in August last year, which I believe illustrates a broader concern. At that time, I initially attended the practice with significant eye symptoms. I was seen by a GP who attempted to arrange a referral. Later the same day, I was contacted by the practice and informed that I would need to wait until specialist appointments became available and that I would be contacted in due course.
As my symptoms were concerning, I subsequently attended the hospital emergency department myself, where I was assessed by the ophthalmology team and formally diagnosed with Horner’s syndrome.
A few days after this diagnosis, I returned to the practice wishing to discuss the condition with a GP. However, I was again booked to see a nurse, without being informed in advance that the appointment would not be with a doctor. During that consultation, the nurse was unfamiliar with Horner’s syndrome, which further reinforced my concern that this was not an appropriate setting for follow-up of a newly diagnosed neurological condition.
I would like to emphasise that I fully respect the role and contribution of nurses within the NHS. My concern relates specifically to the following points:
When I request to see a GP, I am repeatedly booked with a nurse without being informed beforehand that the appointment will not be with a doctor.
In situations involving uncommon or potentially serious diagnoses, such as Horner’s syndrome, I believe it is reasonable to expect review and follow-up by a GP rather than a nurse-led appointment.
To be clear, my concern is not that the nurse did not recognise Horner’s syndrome. Rather, it is that I was not given the opportunity to see a GP, nor was I informed in advance about the nature of the appointment.
